newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm as brokers enter money mkt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm as brokers enter money mkt.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended early firmness at the close of trade on Thursday due to local and foreign brokers switching from dollars to invest in the domestic money market, traders said.
"It is better for brokers to sell their dollars to have pesos to invest at very high rates in the money market," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.05 and two centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8750/7.8775 and 7.8625/7.8650 per dollar.
"As interest rates are so attractive, it is better to go short on dollars, and as that means the peso firms up, you win both ways," the trader said.

Dealers said reduced pressure from the U.S. bond market had also shored up the peso. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 10/32 to yield 7.07 when the foreign exchange market was closing in Mexico. "Dealers are seeing that the time is ripe for switching to pesos. The outlook is still for U.S. rates to go up, but not in the short term," another trader said, referring to the May 20 Federal Open Market Commitee meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed two centavos firmer at 7.8660/7.8700 per dollar.
Dealers estimated the peso could remain at current levels until domestic interest rates begin to decline.

"Some banks are very short on dollars and will stay that way until Banco de Mexico lowers interest rates," a trader said. "But we need to look out for how the central bank intervenes in the secondary money market."
